prompt: Consider a hypothetical 50 Mbit/s satellite link with 600 ms propagation RTT, 1500-byte frames and independent raw bit errors at 10⁻⁵ before FEC. Residual losses remain after coding. Which choices merit consideration for reliable bulk transfer? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use a suitable FEC code to reduce residual errors without a retransmission round trip
options.explanation: Correct. Coding trades redundancy and decoding delay for error correction. Its effectiveness requires a specific code and channel model; it cannot be assumed to fix most errors without analysis.

options.text: Avoid stop-and-wait ARQ, because the sender would sit idle almost all the time
options.explanation: Correct. With 1500-byte frames, each frame takes 0.24 ms to send against a 600 ms RTT: utilisation about 0.04%.

options.text: Consider Selective Repeat to avoid retransmitting later correctly received frames after a gap
options.explanation: Correct. Large windows can make Go-Back-N retransmission waste substantial. Benefit depends on residual loss, memory, processing and timing.

options.text: Use the largest possible frames, since bigger frames always mean less overhead
options.explanation: Under the independent-bit assumption, a 12,000-bit uncoded frame has at least one error with probability about 11.3%. Larger frames increase that probability; the best size depends on overhead, coding and recovery.

options.text: Use 3-bit sequence numbers to keep the header small
options.explanation: 3 bits allow a window of at most 4 frames with Selective Repeat, far below the thousands needed to fill a 600 ms, 50 Mbit/s path.

workedExample:
```formula
L / R = 12,000 bit / (5 × 10⁷ bit/s)
L / R = 0.24 ms
BDP = R RTT = 5 × 10⁷ bit/s × 0.6 s
BDP = 3 × 10⁷ bit = 3.75 MB
N = (0.24 + 600) ms / 0.24 ms = 2,501
U = 0.24 ms / (0.24 ms + 600 ms)
U ≈ 0.0004 = 0.04%
p = 1 − (1 − 10⁻⁵)^12000 ≈ 0.113
where
L: the frame size, 1500 bytes = 12,000 bits
R: the link rate, 50 Mbit/s = 5 × 10⁷ bits per second
bit: one binary digit; bit/s is bits per second
ms: milliseconds, thousandths of a second
s: seconds
BDP: the bandwidth-delay product of the propagation round trip
RTT: the propagation round-trip time, 600 ms = 0.6 s
MB: megabytes; 1 MB is 8,000,000 bits
N: the loss-free window, in frames, that keeps the link busy
U: stop-and-wait utilisation
p: the probability that an uncoded 12,000-bit frame has at least one bit error, with each bit independently wrong with probability 10⁻⁵
≈: approximately equal to
In words: the path holds 2,500 frames in flight (2,501 counting one frame time), stop-and-wait would use only about 0.04% of it, and about 11.3% of uncoded full-size frames would be damaged.
```

A 2,501-frame window still requires at least 13 sequence bits for equal-window Selective Repeat. Suitable FEC can reduce residual errors, and selective retransmission avoids resending later acknowledged frames. These are design calculations, not a validated implementation or measured satellite performance.
